claims.text: Rapidly quenched FeCoNiTi has a dual-phase microstructure comprising an fcc matrix and hexagonal C14 Laves precipitates.
The FeCoNiTi alloy exhibits ferromagnetic ordering transitions near 1084 K, 214 K, and 168 K.
Coexisting C14 Laves phase induces antiferromagnetic exchange coupling between its Ti-rich sublattice and the Fe/Co/Ni-rich fcc matrix.
The proposed interphase coupling suppresses the net saturation magnetization associated with the fcc phase.
The fcc/C14 interfaces create strong interfacial magnetic anisotropy.
The fcc/C14 interfaces act as domain-wall pinning sites.
The dual-phase mechanism raises coercivity to approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
Controlled annealing can systematically vary the C14 phase fraction and hence the fcc/C14 interfacial area while retaining nominal FeCoNiTi composition.
Coupling of Ti 3d states to Fe/Co/Ni 3d states at the interface produces localized spin canting.
Localized interfacial spin canting enhances magnetic anisotropy energy.
The C14 phase is Ti-rich and has an electronic structure distinct from that of the fcc matrix.
Ti moments in the C14 phase couple antiferromagnetically to the ferromagnetic fcc matrix.
Phase decomposition can produce decreased saturation magnetization together with increased coercivity.
Saturation magnetization decreases proportionally as the C14 volume fraction increases.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys have coercivity capped at 100 Oe because of insufficient orbital moments.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni lacks strong domain-wall pinning mechanisms.
The proposed mechanism requires a coherent or semi-coherent fcc/C14 interface.
Laves secondary phases can be intrinsically brittle.
Thermodynamic databases may lack adequate accuracy for predicting phase stability in complex high-entropy alloys.
A spin-polarized DFT interface model comparing the fcc/C14 interface with bulk fcc can test for antiferromagnetic coupling and modification of the spin-resolved density of states at the Fermi level.

contradictions.description: The mechanism attributes domain-wall pinning to incoherent interfaces, whereas the boundary states that the hypothesis requires coherent or semi-coherent interfaces and may fail when the C14 phase forms incoherent precipitates.
